notes:
T326 — GTP handicap surface (set_free_handicap, place_free_handicap, fixed_handicap) so Sabaki can start a handicap game against the oracle. GTP surface only: no solver, no artifact, no rules change — only src/gtp.zig touched. The oracle table covers every reachable (position, side, ko, passes) state, and any legal handicap placement (k Black stones, White to move, no ko, passes=0) is reachable via Black-plays/White-passes alternation, so handicap-start lookups hit the table with no solver change.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED (src/gtp.zig):
- set_free_handicap <vertices>: places the GUI's chosen stones as Black on an empty goban; sets passes=0, ko=none, pushes the handicap position to the PSK history (so it cannot be recreated), resets the sustained-loss FIFOs. Side-to-move is caller-driven in GTP (every play/genmove names a colour), so 'White to move' is conveyed by the protocol, not session state. Rejects (GTP error '?'): board not empty; <2 stones; duplicate vertex; invalid vertex; >legal_max stones. legal_max = w*h-1 (leave >=1 empty point so the game can proceed).
- place_free_handicap <n>: engine chooses n stones by oracle value via the greedy B-move/W-pass walk — for each candidate empty point, place a Black stone and evaluate the (child, Black, ko=none, passes=1) table entry (the state after 'Black plays, White passes'); pick the candidate that maximizes Black's pinned value, commit, repeat. Every evaluated state is a reachable table entry, so lookups hit (0 misses observed). Returns the placed vertices. No new solver machinery.
- fixed_handicap <n>: GTP fixed placements are defined for standard hoshi board sizes only; there are no hoshi on 4x4. Implemented as an alias for place_free_handicap (same greedy placements) so the engine works regardless of which command a GUI sends on a custom-size goban. This is a DEVIATION from the letter of the GTP spec (fixed_handicap should return spec-defined hoshi, not engine-chosen stones) — recorded here as a finding. Sabaki end-to-end verification of which command it actually sends on a custom-size goban is DEFERRED TO THE HUMAN: this automated worker has no GUI access and could not observe Sabaki's GTP console traffic. Implementing fixed_handicap as the greedy alias is the safe choice (works either way); if the human finds Sabaki uses only the free-placement pair, fixed_handicap can be switched to return a GTP error instead.
- All three commands added to KNOWN_COMMANDS (Sabaki feature-detects via list_commands).
- handicapValue helper dispatches WZO2 (bounds2 with explicit ko/passes) vs WZO1 (v0 child lookup, no ko/passes dimension); WZO1 path verified not to crash on the 3x3 artifact.

REGRESSION TEST (inside gtp.zig, 'T326: 2-stone handicap game, 0 misses / 0 fallbacks'): spawns bin/weizigo-gtp with untracked/oracle-v2/oracle-4x4-v2.wzo2, pipes boardsize 4 / set_free_handicap A4 D1 / weizigo_chaincheck w / genmove w / play b C2 / genmove w / weizigo-stats / final_score / quit. Asserts: post-handicap state resolves in the table and is chainable (chaincheck reply contains 'a1=1'); weizigo-stats contains 'misses=0' and 'fallbacks=0'; final_score is a sane score string (B+<n> | W+<n> | 0). All 88 gtp.zig tests pass (zig test src/gtp.zig).

OBSERVED GTP TRAFFIC (4x4 WZO2, engine=White, 2-stone handicap A4 D1):
  boardsize 4               -> =
  set_free_handicap A4 D1   -> =
  weizigo_chaincheck w      -> = a1=1 a2=1 move=B3 v0=-16
  genmove w                 -> = B3
  play b C2                 -> =
  genmove w                 -> = C3
  weizigo-stats             -> = lookups=139 misses=0 fallbacks=0 genmoves=2
  final_score               -> = B+1
The post-handicap state (2 corner Black stones, White to move) is chainable (a1=1) and in the table; the engine's two White genmoves hit the table with 0 misses and 0 fallbacks; final_score B+1 is sane.

FINDING (brief requirement #6, genmove from a handicap start): the engine does NOT enforce the handicap side-to-move convention. genmove <colour> is colour-parameterised and the session tracks no side-to-move (GTP is caller-driven). If the GUI sends genmove b IMMEDIATELY after a handicap (White to move by convention), the engine obligingly moves Black from a state that is UNREACHABLE under correct play — (handicap, Black to move, passes=0) was never explored by the solver, so those lookups MISS and bounds2 falls back to area score. Observed: genmove b first from a 4-stone handicap -> 9 misses, 1 fallback (UNCHAINABLE A1). Correct usage gives 0 misses / 0 fallbacks for BOTH seat assignments: (a) engine=White — genmove w first from the handicap start (White moves first by convention); (b) engine=Black — play w <human> first, THEN genmove b (Black moves after a real White move, a reachable state). Sabaki tracks turns and sends the correct colour, so this is not a field problem, but it IS the 'genmove misbehaves from a handicap start' case the brief asked to flag. No fix applied: the brief scoped this as GTP surface only (no solver/artifact change), and the table correctly does not cover out-of-turn states; the existing area-score fallback keeps the engine functional (not crashed). Recorded as a finding, not a scope excuse.

GREEDY PLACEMENT SHAPE (place_free_handicap, 4x4): the walk fills row-by-row from the top-left corner (A4 B4 C4 D4 then A3 B3 ...) because on a near-symmetric goban early candidates tie on value and the tie-break keeps the lowest colex cell. Values are monotone in k: 2 stones -> v0=-16 (Black losing — 2 stones is an insufficient handicap on 4x4, White to move wins the whole goban), 4 -> v0=1, 6 -> v0=6, 8 -> v0=8, 12 -> v0=16 (White's best is pass), 15 -> v0=16. This is the table's honest fresh-start verdict, not a placement bug.
